newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom leads New Zealand share market down.
newsitem.headline: Telecom leads New Zealand share market down.

text.p: The New Zealand share market closed solidly down on Thursday in a market dominated by Telecom.
The market leader fell 10 cents to NZ$7.20 on hefty volume including two lines of 3.9 million and 1.4 million shares at $7.19.
Brokers said that the large seller would have soaked up all local and institutional demand for some time.
All the leaders except Brierley were weak, with the top 40 index down 15.32 to 2,335.91 on total volume of $104 million.
The market is picked to coast fairly calmly until the New Year holiday with brokers saying it has showed reasonable resilience to volatility in Pacific markets.

"It was a heavier market than we have seen for a few days but reasonably well absorbed at these prices. It's starting to represent slightly better value in the leaders," said County NatWest broker Sean Vaughan.

Fletcher Paper weakened seven cents to $2.72 but its sister company Fletcher Energy was the star of the market after announcing it was proceeding with the US$230 million delevelopment of the Maharaja Lela field in Brunei.
The shares ended 11 cents ahead at $4.02 but had been as much as 24 cents up.
Analysts said the field news was significant for Fletcher as a credibility issue to its development programme.
There was a line of 5.4 million Wang traded at $2.21, 19 cents below its previous price, which had brokers puzzled.
